target_customer: Retail and restaurant employers and their hourly employees who coordinate shifts
problem: Hourly workers swap shifts and talk to managers through text threads, phone calls and Facebook groups. Shift offered a messaging and shift swap tool built for scheduling.
business_model: B2B SaaS for retail and restaurant employers

founders.name: Austin Vedder
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists Vedder Family (investor) and says he was Redbeacon's first non-founding hire.

founders.name: Matt Tognetti
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says both founders previously worked at Redbeacon, which Home Depot later acquired.

exit.reason: YC lists Inactive. One profile of Vedder says Snagajob acquired the company in December 2017, but no second source confirms it.

competitors.name: ShiftSmart
competitors.what: Shift scheduling and swap app for shift workers

competitors.name: Text threads and Facebook groups
competitors.what: Informal tools hourly workers already use to swap shifts

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile messaging and shift swap app is standard engineering. The hard part was adoption among managers and employees, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Value grows when a whole store's staff is on the app, but incumbent schedulers and simple chat tools could copy shift swapping quickly.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying Shift. A single unconfirmed profile claims Snagajob acquired it in December 2017.

market_need_then: TechCrunch and Version One describe hourly workers coordinating through calls, texts and Facebook groups instead of tools made for them. Retail turnover and manager time spent on scheduling were the stated pain points.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the launch and seed, but no source shows brand assets or community. The word Shift is generic and shared by many unrelated companies, which made it confusable.

outcome_analysis: Shift Messenger launched in February 2015 after YC Winter 2015 and raised a 1.5M seed in May 2015 from a strong set of seed funds. The company is now inactive, and the only claim about its end is an unconfirmed single profile that Snagajob acquired it in 2017. The cause of the end is not public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: YC lists no website, so there was no company site to fetch (dead or absent). Seed round amount comes from TechCrunch; the Version One post cross-checks the date and lead investor but states no amount. The Snagajob acquisition rests on one profile page and is unverified. A search for dated competitors also surfaced When I Work, Snagajob and HotSchedules, which are not listed because no pre-batch dated source was opened. Social posts of the same year were not checked.
